paragraphs: Rabbi Abba bar Abba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: “One may urinate in public, but one may not drink water in public. Someone wished to urinate and did not, and his belly was found swollen,” chapter Mumin, Bekhorot 44b. Perhaps this is an error and should be Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba. In a gloss Yuchasin writes, “Sh.Sh. said: Perhaps he is Shmuel’s father,” who was called Abba bar Abba. “The evidence is that Bekhorot there says Shmuel was lecturing and wished to urinate; he ordered a cloth brought as a screen and urinated. His father took exception and ordered him to teach that it is permitted even without a screen. He went out and taught: One may urinate in public.” End quotation. The Gemara does not have “He went out and taught,” etc. Yet the matter requires examination: we do not find Abba bar Abba, Shmuel’s father, reporting in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. Our reading, however, is: Rabbi Abba son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name.
